Let $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ be two stations attempting to transmit on an Ethernet. Each has frames ready to send all the time; $\text{A's}$ frames will be numbered $\text{A1, A2}$, and so on, and $\text{B's}$ similarly. At the end of this transmission, $\text{B}$ will attempt to retransmit $\text{B} 1$ while $\text{A}$ will attempt to transmit $\text{A} 2$. These attempts will collide, but now $\text{A}$ backs off for either $0 \times \mathrm{T}$ or $1 \times \mathrm{T}$, while $\text{B}$ backs off for time equal to one of $0 \times \mathrm{T}, \ldots, 3 \times \mathrm{T}$.

questions.qtext:
Consider the hosts $\text{W, X, Y, Z}$ and the learning bridges $\text{B1, B2, B3}.$ Assume, that they have empty forwarding tables to begin.

Suppose the following two events happens in the order.

  1. Host $\text{X}$ sends a packet to $\text{W}$
  2. Host $\text{Z}$ sends a packet to $\text{Y}.$

Now, finally, host $\text{W}$ sends to $\text{Y}.$ Which of the following is/are true for this last transmission?

options.text: Bridge $\text{B2}$ will learn of the location of $\text{W}.$
Bridge $\text{B3}$ will learn of the location of $\text{W}.$

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C, D
